groups.title: Type-two causative foundation
groups.proposal: Let the user choose a type-two causative and select an underlying nonactive Source history only when more than one licensed history remains possible; then derive the one-, two-, or three-object result through the normal causative composition path.
groups.writingJob: Consume an open typed Source and its owner-issued nonactive history, derive tiā from the nonactive base, preserve unexpected or reconstructed histories, allow parallel licensed histories, and automatically use the Canvas-required huīca suppletion for yāuh and huāllāuh.
groups.readingJob: Explain tiā as empty ti plus causative ā, the hua, ā, o-hua, and lō source families, possible honorific-only use, ambiguous tiā versus meaningful ti-ā, and the irregular go/come suppletion without turning the examples into an admission list.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses Causative Type 2 and only resolves a real choice among licensed Source histories. The application derives the target valence, causative cluster, participant structure, and required suppletion.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Derivation and the compact Source-history choice; do not add controls for object count, ti plus ā composition, nonactive deletion, honorific notes, or example identity.

groups.title: Hua-source routes and shape changes
groups.proposal: When a typed Source uses a hua nonactive history, replace hua with tiā and derive the visible vowel and consonant changes from Source shape; expose an alternative i-hui or a-hui history only when the intended analysis really permits more than one causative formation.
groups.writingJob: Apply hua-to-tiā replacement to an open Source, derive long or shortened i and the licensed a-to-i, s-to-x, and postvocalic ti-to-chi outcomes, preserve supportive i, keep i-hui and a-hui Type 1 or Type 2 alternatives available, and derive causative valence from Source valence.
groups.readingJob: Show the hidden hua history, reconstructed intermediates, consonant-cluster shortening, meanings, reflexive examples, unattested counterparts, and all Canvas witnesses as guidance rather than a stem whitelist.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies the Source and its intended valence and chooses among genuinely licensed Source histories or parallel formations only when unresolved. The application performs every regular shape change and participant consequence.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Source Valence, Causative Type, and a short Source-history choice; do not add controls for vowel length, shortening, supportive vowels, consonant changes, listed stems, or example meanings.

groups.title: O and o-hua Sources, machtia, and silent shuntlines
groups.proposal: Replace o or o-hua with tiā from the selected Source history, preserve genuine machtia source ambiguity, and let a qualified writer choose silent versus sounded specific shuntline realization only where Andrews actually licenses both.
groups.writingJob: Derive the consonant-before-tiā route, block the two-consonant environment and redirect l to the lō route, preserve the special machtia object restrictions and reflexive or reciprocal readings, keep silent objects fully grammatical and supplementable, and apply the w and m boundary changes.
groups.readingJob: Explain the o and o-hua histories, machtia's intransitive/transitive readings, specific-object restriction, silent shuntline, ambiguity resolution by supplementation, author variation, and the unexpected w- and m-final examples.
groups.decisionSplit: For composition, the user chooses the intended Source history and resolves a real reflexive/reciprocal or intransitive/transitive interpretation; a silent-versus-sounded shuntline choice appears only in the licensed author-variation environment. For reading, unresolved ambiguity remains visible.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Source history, participant identity, supplementation, and one conditional shuntline-realization choice; do not add controls for consonant cues, silent-object reality, supplement heads, or Canvas examples.

groups.title: Lō-source routes and their alternations
groups.proposal: Use the selected lō history to replace only its final ō with tiā, retain l, and derive each shape-conditioned alternation automatically; show a choice only for genuinely parallel licensed histories.
groups.writingJob: Build the l-tiā result from an open typed lō Source, cover Class C and D Sources, derive ka/ki, ni/na, kwa/i, s/x, wa/wi, and ti/chi alternations, and preserve licensed root-plus-ya variants.
groups.readingJob: Expose the lō bridge, retained l, reconstructed intermediates, unexpected formations, semantic contrasts, and example histories as clickable guidance.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses an unresolved licensed Source history or variant; the application derives the retained l, sound changes, participants, and target form.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the Source-history choice; do not add a separate control for each sound alternation or example stem.

groups.title: Liā causatives
groups.proposal: Allow a causative liā analysis for a typed denominal ti Source or root-plus-ya Source and distinguish it from the identical applicative liā only when the intended construction is genuinely ambiguous.
groups.writingJob: Attach liā to denominal ti Sources, replace root-plus-ya with root plus liā, preserve typed deverbal histories, and route the result through the shared causative participant transformation.
groups.readingJob: Show the denominal and root-plus-ya source structure, literal and lexical meanings, applicative homophony, exceptions, and examples without a stem list.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses Causative versus Applicative when the same liā shape supports both and confirms a Source history only if needed. The application derives deletion, participants, and result class.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Derivation and Source history; do not add denominal, ya-deletion, class, or example controls.

groups.title: Huiā, Class C, and parallel causatives
groups.proposal: Let a typed long-o Source take direct huiā, o-to-a plus huiā, or an lō-to-tiā history when licensed, and let the user choose Type 1 versus Type 2 or Causative versus Applicative only where the same Source genuinely supports both.
groups.writingJob: Derive direct and replacive huiā routes, preserve an alternative lō bridge, assign every tiā, liā, and huiā causative to Class C, and keep parallel Type 1 and Type 2 results distinct.
groups.readingJob: Explain huiā homophony, matching or divergent meanings of parallel causatives, and the Canvas examples without making their stems authoritative.
groups.decisionSplit: The user resolves licensed derivation-role or history ambiguity. The application derives the target shape, class, participants, and parallel-result cues.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Derivation Type and Source history; do not add a Class C, meaning-match, or example control.

groups.title: Basic transformation and single-object causatives
groups.proposal: Reuse the normal causative transformation: the user supplies the new causer and chooses reflexive identity only when it is a real referent decision; the application compacts the Source, transfers its subject, and derives the object form from Source voice.
groups.writingJob: Replace the Source stem, convert its subject to specific, reflexive, or nonspecific causative object, import the new subject, and keep the causee object-like in form but subject-like in the embedded event.
groups.readingJob: Show each participant transfer, literal versus lexical readings, shared translations, and active or impersonal Source evidence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the imported causer and any real coreference. The application derives causative-object specificity and all pronoun shapes.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Subject and participant-identity controls; do not ask for object-pronoun shape or transformation steps.

groups.title: Double-object causatives
groups.proposal: Build double-object causatives from the typed active-transitive, passive, or impersonal Source; let the user choose participant identity, while mainline promotion, shuntline order, silence, ne, and coreference shapes are automatic.
groups.writingJob: Promote the causative object to mainline, preserve the Source object on the shuntline, enforce specific-object compatibility, convert source reflexive or reciprocal m-o to ne unless coreference requires n-o or m-o, and derive passive or impersonal agent transfer.
groups.readingJob: Show source voice, mainline and shuntline roles, silent specific objects, ne replacement, coreference exceptions, conative and lexical readings, and all examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the Source, new causer, and genuine referent identities. The application derives all object levels and visible or silent pronoun shapes.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Source Voice and participant identity; do not expose mainline, shuntline, silence, ne, or prefix-order controls.

groups.title: Triple-object causatives
groups.proposal: Recapture a typed double-object causative as the Source for one more causative layer and derive the mainline plus two shuntline levels automatically from participant roles and Source voice.
groups.writingJob: Create specific, reflexive, and nonspecific mainline outcomes, preserve second- and first-level shuntline functions, realize licensed silent objects, and apply coreference exceptions without a separate triple-object engine.
groups.readingJob: Expose all three object levels, their functions, silent realizations, recursive Source, literal and lexical readings, and the non-exhaustive status of examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user selects the recursive Source, new causer, and genuine participant identity. The application derives ordering, levels, silence, and voice consequences.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse recursive causative composition and participant identity; do not add manual object-level or prefix-order controls.

groups.title: Multiple-source ambiguity
groups.proposal: Preserve every grammatically possible Source analysis for an ambiguous multiple-object result and ask the user to select one only when producing an intended composition or when context truly resolves the reading.
groups.writingJob: Generate all licensed sources without using surface strings as authority, keep fixed prefix order, apply specific-object incompatibility and ne replacement, and preserve unresolved ambiguity in Result analysis.
groups.readingJob: Present the competing Source analyses, contextual interpretations, ambiguity reducers, and examples as concise clickable alternatives.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses an intended Source for composition or a context-supported reading; the application never silently discards another licensed analysis.
groups.controlPolicy: Use one conditional Source-analysis choice; do not ask the user to label prefix functions already settled by a selected Source.

groups.title: Moods, passive, and impersonal voice
groups.proposal: Let ordinary Mood and Voice controls apply to a completed causative VNC, then derive optative, command or exhortation, admonitive, passive, and impersonal results through their shared canonical owners.
groups.writingJob: Feed the causative result into the existing mood and nonactive-voice transformations while preserving its remaining objects and participant hierarchy.
groups.readingJob: Show assertion-to-mood and active-to-passive or impersonal comparisons, formula roles, lexical readings, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses Mood or Voice. The application derives all form changes and retained participant roles.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Mood and Voice; do not add Lesson-25-specific sentence or passive controls.

groups.title: Supplementing silent causative objects
groups.proposal: Reuse Lesson 17 supplementation so any grammatically present silent direct or shuntline object can serve as a supplement head and the supplement can clarify its referent without making it overt in the principal.
groups.writingJob: Authorize a supplement link to the typed silent object, validate referent identity, preserve the object's level and silence, and use the supplement's subject to clarify person or number when supplied.
groups.readingJob: Show the principal, silent head, supplement, cross-reference link, clarified referent, and all three Canvas examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses which eligible silent object the supplement targets only when more than one is available and supplies the supplement. The application derives cross-reference and interpretation.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the compact Lesson 17 supplement-head choice and nested-link cues; do not add a Lesson-25-specific supplementation workflow.
